title: sporobolus indicus var. laxus
intro: Sporobolus indicus var. laxus, commonly known as Indian grass, is a type of grass native to India and other parts of Asia. The plant has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat various health conditions, including inflammation, fever, and respiratory issues. The health benefits of Indian grass include its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to reduce pain, improve wound healing, and protect against oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of Indian grass include flavonoids, glycosides, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects.
